Based on the healthcare Q&A matches provided, it appears that serum samples may not be the most suitable choice for analyzing the EGFR (epidermal growth factor receptor) mutation status in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer.

While serum can be used as a preliminary test to detect elevated levels of certain biomarkers, including EGFR protein expression, this is not considered a reliable or definitive method for diagnosing EGFR mutation status. The completion notes from the Q&A matches suggest that there may be difficulties in obtaining tumor tissue for analysis, making serum testing a challenging aspect of diagnosis.

In fact, the completion notes also mention that other methods, such as immunohistochemistry (IHC) and sequencing analyses using techniques like SSCP (single-strand conformation polymorphism), are more reliable for detecting EGFR mutations. Additionally, some completion notes note that the levels of certain biomarkers, including leptin, may not have prognostic value in advanced non-small cell lung cancer.

It's worth noting that while serum testing may be used as a supplement to diagnosis or monitoring, it is not a replacement for more definitive diagnostic methods like IHC and sequencing analyses. If you are considering testing for EGFR mutation status, it's essential to discuss your specific situation with a healthcare professional who can guide you through the best testing options and ensure that any testing is performed in accordance with current guidelines and best practices.
